claims.text: Rapid solidification produces a high dislocation density in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Rapidly solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn has a fine-grained microstructure.
Rapidly solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn contains uniformly distributed nanometer-scale Mn-rich oxide precipitates.
The dynamic mechanical response of solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed synergistically by its high dislocation density and Mn-rich oxide precipitates.
At low temperatures or slow strain rates, the Mn-rich oxide precipitates strengthen FeNiCrMn through Orowan looping.
A high dislocation density provides forest-type strengthening and increased strain hardening in FeNiCrMn.
Low-temperature or low-strain-rate deformation produces high yield strength and work hardening but relatively low ductility.
Increasing temperature lowers the yield strength of the rapidly solidified alloy.
Elevated temperature increases dislocation mobility in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Elevated-temperature deformation can produce dynamic recovery or partial dynamic recrystallization.
Higher strain rates promote partial dynamic recovery or recrystallization in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Dynamic recovery or recrystallization reduces dislocation- and precipitate-based strengthening.
Elevated temperatures and higher strain rates improve the ductility of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Low-temperature deformation will produce pronounced interactions between dislocations and Mn-rich oxide precipitates.
As-solidified FeNiCrMn has high strength and moderate ductility under quasi-static conditions.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to rapidly solidified FeNiCrMn between approximately 25 °C and 900 °C at moderate strain rates.
Ultra-high strain rates or post-annealed and coarsened microstructures may activate additional deformation mechanisms.
